A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 20-page versions of the same study. All seven figures, three tables, and Appendices A–D are available, and relocated or renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments across eight classification datasets, including learning curves, performance break-even measurements, and model-size and quantisation analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 3, Table 1, and Appendices B–C, with the in-context-learning quantisation figure moved into the main text.

M1.justification: The fine-tuning, instruction-tuning, prompting, and in-context-learning procedures remain unchanged. Section 3 and Appendix A.2 retain the same training objectives, components, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use SST2, MRPC, CoLA, BoolQ, AG News, TREC, SNIPS, and DB Pedia for the same English classification tasks. No dataset, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same eight models participate in the corresponding comparisons. GPT is relabelled GPT-4 in several passages, but both versions specify the same 4o-mini-2024-07-18 snapshot; this is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains the 60/20/20 splits, training-subset sweep, macro-F1 metric, and training and inference settings. The restricted 1,000-sample test evaluations and selection of the best preceding in-context-learning performance are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The model-size, dataset-dependence, and quantisation analyses are retained. The expanded Section 3.3 summarises existing appendix evidence, and v3 Figure 7 becomes v4 Figure 4 without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Both report 100 fine-tuning runs, 20 runs for other approaches with a 10-run GPT exception, and macro-F1 means and standard deviations. Seed handling and the variance-based break-even calculation remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All three tables retain identical contents, and the matched figures retain their plotted results. For example, Table 1 still reports SST2 fine-tuning-versus-prompting break-even sizes of 350 and 900 samples. Added summary statements already appear in v3's appendices.

T1.justification: The definitions of the two break-even points and the comparison using means plus or minus standard deviations are unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal empirical contributions remain unchanged. Section 5 removes extremely limited computation budget from its explicit examples of when general models are advantageous, retaining quick prototyping and extremely limited annotation.

C2.justification: The conclusion no longer explicitly presents limited computation alone as a favourable use case for general models. This is a limited applicability refinement: Section 4's detailed budget discussion and the stated limitations remain unchanged, while Section 3.3 repeats existing appendix interpretations.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 replaces the anonymous code-repository link with the named GitHub repository kinit-sk/L3D-sensitivity-investigation. This changes documented code-access information; Appendix A's implementation details and Appendix D's hardware and computation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. Pecher et al. (2024a) is updated from its arXiv preprint entry to its EMNLP proceedings entry, representing the same work.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 expands its summary using findings already documented in Appendices B–C. Local wording, model-label, acknowledgement, and bibliographic edits accompany this expansion, while the overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves its legend below the plot into a larger, two-column arrangement. The appendix quantisation plot, v3 Figure 7, becomes main-text Figure 4 in v4, producing figure renumbering and page reflow. The detailed plots and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The clearer Figure 1 legend and main-text placement of the existing quantisation comparison make the findings easier to follow, while the code footnote identifies a named repository. These provide modest readability and documentation gains. Experiments and results remain unchanged, and Section 3.3 introduces some repetition, limiting the overall improvement.
